{"query":"link no telemetry collector gap versus link down","results":[{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":4.524,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.518,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":5.248,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

{"query":"link no telemetry collector gap versus link down, services unreachable","results":[{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":4.762,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.755,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

Fault type: link_flapping. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface goes down and up repeatedly; several short link_status_down alerts on the same link, or intermittent gaps in its telemetry.
- Repeated short bursts of loss on services that cross the link as routing converges each time.
- Utilisation on the link drops and recovers repeatedly; neighbours show matching opposite swings.

"},{"runbook":"RB07_routing_misconfig","score":1.437,"text":"# RB07 Routing misconfiguration (link metric change)

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.
- If a link lost most of its traffic while staying up, and nothing is logged, the metric on that link is the likely root.
- If one link suddenly carries much more than the day before, check whether paths were pulled onto it.

Action: compare the running routing metric with the intended configuration; roll back the change.

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.

Action: compare the running routing metric with the intended configuration; roll back the change.
"},{"runbook":"RB08_maintenance_and_drains","score":2.597,"text":"# RB08 Planned maintenance and drains (general)

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.
- A no-op entry is logged work that did not touch traffic.
- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.
"}]}

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.

"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.518,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

{"query":"link_no_data telemetry missing collector gap versus link down","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":8.736,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":5.232,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

{"query":"link no data telemetry gap versus link down with traffic shift to parallel link","results":[{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":5.146,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.747,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

{"query":"link_no_data telemetry gap collector blanked versus link down","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":6.383,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":5.76,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

{"query":"link no data telemetry gap versus link down; util saturation discards reroute","results":[{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":4.872,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.415,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

calls.output:
{"query":"routing misconfig metric changed on one link traffic pulled onto link saturates without change log","results":[{"runbook":"RB07_routing_misconfig","score":11.15,"text":"# RB07 Routing misconfiguration (link metric change)

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.
- If a link lost most of its traffic while staying up, and nothing is logged, the metric on that link is the likely root.
- If one link suddenly carries much more than the day before, check whether paths were pulled onto it.

Action: compare the running routing metric with the intended configuration; roll back the change.
"},{"runbook":"RB08_maintenance_and_drains","score":5.117,"text":"# RB08 Planned maintenance and drains (general)

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.
- A no-op entry is logged work that did not touch traffic.
- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.
"}]}

{"query":"link no telemetry link_no_data collector gap versus link down","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":6.478,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":4.524,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

{"query":"link_no_data telemetry missing link down vs collector gap","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":8.736,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":5.232,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

{"query":"link down status probe fail diagnosis","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":3.577,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":3.438,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

{"query":"link no telemetry collector gap versus link down, traffic rerouted causing congestion","results":[{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":5.777,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.755,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:

- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

{"query":"router node down all links no telemetry reroute","results":[{"runbook":"RB03_node_down","score":3.995,"text":"# RB03 Router (PoP) down

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:
- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.
- Every link attached to the router goes dark or reads zero at the same time.
- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

Checks:
- Do all links of one PoP show the same outage at the same step? A single dark link is a link fault; all links of one router is the router.
- Is there a planned outage on the PoP in the change log?

Action: dispatch to the site; check power and control plane; confirm traffic has moved to alternate paths.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":3.302,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:
- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.

- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

"},{"runbook":"RB06_demand_surge","score":6.23,"text":"# RB06 Demand surge at a PoP

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.

{"query":"PoP unreachable with all attached links down: node down vs link down distinction","results":[{"runbook":"RB03_node_down","score":9.378,"text":"# RB03 Router (PoP) down

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:
- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.
- Every link attached to the router goes dark or reads zero at the same time.
- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

Checks:
- Do all links of one PoP show the same outage at the same step? A single dark link is a link fault; all links of one router is the router.
- Is there a planned outage on the PoP in the change log?

Action: dispatch to the site; check power and control plane; confirm traffic has moved to alternate paths.
"},{"runbook":"RB06_demand_surge","score":4.413,"text":"# RB06 Demand surge at a PoP

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.
"}]}

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.

{"query":"link no telemetry vs node down single-homed PoP unreachable","results":[{"runbook":"RB03_node_down","score":6.306,"text":"# RB03 Router (PoP) down

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:
- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.
- Every link attached to the router goes dark or reads zero at the same time.
- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

Checks:
- Do all links of one PoP show the same outage at the same step? A single dark link is a link fault; all links of one router is the router.
- Is there a planned outage on the PoP in the change log?

Action: dispatch to the site; check power and control plane; confirm traffic has moved to alternate paths.
"},{"runbook":"RB06_demand_surge","score":3.514,"text":"# RB06 Demand surge at a PoP

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.
"}]}

{"query":"link no telemetry collector gap versus node down New Orleans","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.423,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.

"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":4.418,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":5.92,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:
- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.

- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.

- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:

"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":4.32,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.
- If a link lost most of its traffic while staying up, and nothing is logged, the metric on that link is the likely root.
- If one link suddenly carries much more than the day before, check whether paths were pulled onto it.

Action: compare the running routing metric with the intended configuration; roll back the change.
"},{"runbook":"RB08_maintenance_and_drains","score":2.462,"text":"# RB08 Planned maintenance and drains (general)

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.
- A no-op entry is logged work that did not touch traffic.
- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.

Fault type: link_flapping. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface goes down and up repeatedly; several short link_status_down alerts on the same link, or intermittent gaps in its telemetry.
- Repeated short bursts of loss on services that cross the link as routing converges each time.
- Utilisation on the link drops and recovers repeatedly; neighbours show matching opposite swings.

Checks:
- Count down/up episodes on the link in the window: more than one short episode is the signature.
- Rule out a collector problem: intermittent gaps on many unrelated links at once are not flapping.

Action: dampen or shut the interface and reroute; check optics and physical layer.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":3.814,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.

Fault type: link_flapping. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface goes down and up repeatedly; several short link_status_down alerts on the same link, or intermittent gaps in its telemetry.
- Repeated short bursts of loss on services that cross the link as routing converges each time.
- Utilisation on the link drops and recovers repeatedly; neighbours show matching opposite swings.

- Rule out a collector problem: intermittent gaps on many unrelated links at once are not flapping.

"},{"runbook":"RB05_link_degradation","score":4.062,"text":"# RB05 Link degradation (loss or latency)

Fault type: link_degradation. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The link stays up, but its one-hop latency rises (link_latency_high) or it drops packets (link_discards).
- Services crossing the link breach latency or loss SLAs; services not crossing it are fine.
- Utilisation is often unchanged, because routing does not move traffic away from a degraded but up link.

- Compare the link's latency and discards with the same window one day earlier.
- Find the element shared by the paths of the services with SLA alerts; a degraded link is usually on all of them.
- Small degradations may raise no alert: look at the telemetry of links on the shared paths even without alerts.

Action: raise with the transmission team; consider moving traffic off the link with a metric change.

{"query":"interface status down but traffic still flowing util, poller false positive vs link down","results":[{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":3.989,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":3.849,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"}]}

Fault type: link_degradation. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The link stays up, but its one-hop latency rises (link_latency_high) or it drops packets (link_discards).
- Services crossing the link breach latency or loss SLAs; services not crossing it are fine.
- Utilisation is often unchanged, because routing does not move traffic away from a degraded but up link.

- Compare the link's latency and discards with the same window one day earlier.
- Find the element shared by the paths of the services with SLA alerts; a degraded link is usually on all of them.

Action: raise with the transmission team; consider moving traffic off the link with a metric change.
"},{"runbook":"RB07_routing_misconfig","score":1.435,"text":"# RB07 Routing misconfiguration (link metric change)

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.
- If a link lost most of its traffic while staying up, and nothing is logged, the metric on that link is the likely root.
- If one link suddenly carries much more than the day before, check whether paths were pulled onto it.

Action: compare the running routing metric with the intended configuration; roll back the change.
"}]}

{"query":"planned link outage maintenance service unreachable probe loss after restoration","results":[{"runbook":"RB08_maintenance_and_drains","score":5.215,"text":"# RB08 Planned maintenance and drains (general)

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.
- A no-op entry is logged work that did not touch traffic.
- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":4.512,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.

{"query":"planned outage link down services unreachable maintenance window alerts","results":[{"runbook":"RB08_maintenance_and_drains","score":5.807,"text":"# RB08 Planned maintenance and drains (general)

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.
- A no-op entry is logged work that did not touch traffic.
- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.
"},{"runbook":"RB01_triage","score":4.571,"text":"# RB01 Incident triage (general)

Applies to: every incident. Fault types: all.

1. Read the alert list for the window. Group alerts by element. Service alerts (svc_loss_sla, svc_latency_sla, svc_unreachable) are symptoms seen at the edge; link and router alerts point closer to the cause.
2. Check the change log before anything else. A planned drain, outage or other change on an element in or just before the window explains alerts on that element and on links that took its rerouted traffic.
3. For each candidate element, look at its telemetry in the window against the same window one day earlier. A real fault changes something that was normal the day before.
4. Use the topology: a single root usually explains several symptoms. Find the element shared by the paths of the alerted services (shared elements), and check its neighbours.
5. Decide between: a fault (name the root element and type), planned maintenance only, or no fault. Do not report a fault when every symptom is explained by a logged change.
6. Evidence must quote element ids and values exactly as the tools returned them.
"}]}

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.
"},{"runbook":"RB05_link_degradation","score":4.284,"text":"# RB05 Link degradation (loss or latency)

Fault type: link_degradation. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The link stays up, but its one-hop latency rises (link_latency_high) or it drops packets (link_discards).
- Services crossing the link breach latency or loss SLAs; services not crossing it are fine.
- Utilisation is often unchanged, because routing does not move traffic away from a degraded but up link.

Checks:
- Compare the link's latency and discards with the same window one day earlier.
- Find the element shared by the paths of the services with SLA alerts; a degraded link is usually on all of them.
- Small degradations may raise no alert: look at the telemetry of links on the shared paths even without alerts.

Action: raise with the transmission team; consider moving traffic off the link with a metric change.

{"query":"link discards after planned drain ends, undrain, interface errors","results":[{"runbook":"RB08_maintenance_and_drains","score":3.688,"text":"# RB08 Planned maintenance and drains (general)

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.
- A no-op entry is logged work that did not touch traffic.
- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":2.634,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

Fault type: link_flapping. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface goes down and up repeatedly; several short link_status_down alerts on the same link, or intermittent gaps in its telemetry.

{"query":"interface discards increase with moderate utilization link degradation","results":[{"runbook":"RB05_link_degradation","score":3.953,"text":"# RB05 Link degradation (loss or latency)

Fault type: link_degradation. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The link stays up, but its one-hop latency rises (link_latency_high) or it drops packets (link_discards).
- Services crossing the link breach latency or loss SLAs; services not crossing it are fine.
- Utilisation is often unchanged, because routing does not move traffic away from a degraded but up link.

Checks:
- Compare the link's latency and discards with the same window one day earlier.
- Find the element shared by the paths of the services with SLA alerts; a degraded link is usually on all of them.
- Small degradations may raise no alert: look at the telemetry of links on the shared paths even without alerts.

Action: raise with the transmission team; consider moving traffic off the link with a metric change.
"},{"runbook":"RB04_link_flapping","score":1.702,"text":"# RB04 Link flapping

Fault type: link_flapping. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface goes down and up repeatedly; several short link_status_down alerts on the same link, or intermittent gaps in its telemetry.
- Repeated short bursts of loss on services that cross the link as routing converges each time.
- Utilisation on the link drops and recovers repeatedly; neighbours show matching opposite swings.

Checks:
- Count down/up episodes on the link in the window: more than one short episode is the signature.
- Rule out a collector problem: intermittent gaps on many unrelated links at once are not flapping.

Action: dampen or shut the interface and reroute; check optics and physical layer.
"}]}

Fault type: link_degradation. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The link stays up, but its one-hop latency rises (link_latency_high) or it drops packets (link_discards).
- Services crossing the link breach latency or loss SLAs; services not crossing it are fine.
- Utilisation is often unchanged, because routing does not move traffic away from a degraded but up link.

Checks:

"},{"runbook":"RB07_routing_misconfig","score":4.611,"text":"# RB07 Routing misconfiguration (link metric change)

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.
- If a link lost most of its traffic while staying up, and nothing is logged, the metric on that link is the likely root.
- If one link suddenly carries much more than the day before, check whether paths were pulled onto it.

Action: compare the running routing metric with the intended configuration; roll back the change.

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:
- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.

- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

"},{"runbook":"RB06_demand_surge","score":5.642,"text":"# RB06 Demand surge at a PoP

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.

{"query":"link telemetry missing no data alerts and service unreachable, node down vs collector gap","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":8.826,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":7.282,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

"},{"runbook":"RB07_routing_misconfig","score":3.189,"text":"# RB07 Routing misconfiguration (link metric change)

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.
- If a link lost most of its traffic while staying up, and nothing is logged, the metric on that link is the likely root.
- If one link suddenly carries much more than the day before, check whether paths were pulled onto it.

Action: compare the running routing metric with the intended configuration; roll back the change.

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.
"},{"runbook":"RB05_link_degradation","score":4.819,"text":"# RB05 Link degradation (loss or latency)

Fault type: link_degradation. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The link stays up, but its one-hop latency rises (link_latency_high) or it drops packets (link_discards).
- Services crossing the link breach latency or loss SLAs; services not crossing it are fine.
- Utilisation is often unchanged, because routing does not move traffic away from a degraded but up link.

Checks:
- Compare the link's latency and discards with the same window one day earlier.
- Find the element shared by the paths of the services with SLA alerts; a degraded link is usually on all of them.
- Small degradations may raise no alert: look at the telemetry of links on the shared paths even without alerts.

Action: raise with the transmission team; consider moving traffic off the link with a metric change.

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).

Symptoms:

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:

"},{"runbook":"RB08_maintenance_and_drains","score":4.927,"text":"# RB08 Planned maintenance and drains (general)

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.
- A no-op entry is logged work that did not touch traffic.
- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.
"}]}

{"query":"demand surge signature utilization rise on all links of one router","results":[{"runbook":"RB06_demand_surge","score":6.967,"text":"# RB06 Demand surge at a PoP

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.
"},{"runbook":"RB03_node_down","score":2.61,"text":"# RB03 Router (PoP) down

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:
- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.
- Every link attached to the router goes dark or reads zero at the same time.
- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

Checks:
- Do all links of one PoP show the same outage at the same step? A single dark link is a link fault; all links of one router is the router.
- Is there a planned outage on the PoP in the change log?

Action: dispatch to the site; check power and control plane; confirm traffic has moved to alternate paths.

Fault type: demand_surge. Root: a PoP (the source of the extra traffic).

Symptoms:
- Utilisation rises together on several links attached to one PoP, ramping up over some steps rather than jumping.
- Downstream links on paths from that PoP may hit high utilisation (link_util_high) and start to discard.
- Latency and loss rise on services from that PoP once links congest.

Checks:
- Do the busiest links share one end router? The shared router is the root, not the busiest single link.
- Is the rise larger than the normal daily pattern? Compare with the same window one day earlier.
- A drain in the change log also raises utilisation on neighbouring links; check that first.

Action: identify the traffic source; apply rate limits or add capacity; reroute where possible.
"},{"runbook":"RB05_link_degradation","score":3.005,"text":"# RB05 Link degradation (loss or latency)

Fault type: link_degradation. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The link stays up, but its one-hop latency rises (link_latency_high) or it drops packets (link_discards).
- Services crossing the link breach latency or loss SLAs; services not crossing it are fine.
- Utilisation is often unchanged, because routing does not move traffic away from a degraded but up link.

Checks:
- Compare the link's latency and discards with the same window one day earlier.
- Find the element shared by the paths of the services with SLA alerts; a degraded link is usually on all of them.
- Small degradations may raise no alert: look at the telemetry of links on the shared paths even without alerts.

Action: raise with the transmission team; consider moving traffic off the link with a metric change.

{"query":"pop unreachable versus link_no_data collector gap node down","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":5.558,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB03_node_down","score":5.335,"text":"# RB03 Router (PoP) down

Fault type: node_down. Root: a PoP (router).

Symptoms:
- The router stops answering polls (pop_unreachable) when status polling exists.
- Every link attached to the router goes dark or reads zero at the same time.
- Services that start or end at the PoP become unreachable; services that transited it reroute.

Checks:
- Do all links of one PoP show the same outage at the same step? A single dark link is a link fault; all links of one router is the router.
- Is there a planned outage on the PoP in the change log?

Action: dispatch to the site; check power and control plane; confirm traffic has moved to alternate paths.

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).

"},{"runbook":"RB08_maintenance_and_drains","score":3.13,"text":"# RB08 Planned maintenance and drains (general)

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.
- A no-op entry is logged work that did not touch traffic.
- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.

Applies to: incidents that overlap a change-log entry.

- A drain raises the routing metric of a link so traffic leaves it before work starts. The drained link's utilisation falls; neighbours carry more. Latency on rerouted services can rise. Nothing is broken.
- A planned outage ("down") takes a link or router down on purpose. Telemetry on it stops or reads zero, exactly as in a real failure, and status alerts fire.

- During and just after a change window, alerts on the changed element and on links that took its traffic are expected.

How to decide:
- If every alerted element is the changed element or carries its rerouted traffic, and nothing else is abnormal, the answer is planned maintenance, not a fault.
- A fault can still happen during maintenance: look for symptoms on elements the change does not explain.
- Do not blame the changed element for symptoms that started before the change window.

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:

- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

{"query":"link_probe_fail one-hop probe missing while interface counters present","results":[{"runbook":"RB09_telemetry_gaps","score":9.622,"text":"# RB09 Telemetry gaps and collector problems (general)

Applies to: alerts of type link_no_data or link_probe_fail, and missing values in series.

- Missing telemetry is not a fault by itself. Collectors drop data for single links or for every link of one router for a few steps.
- A down link also stops reporting. Tell them apart:
  - A collector gap is usually short and often hits several unrelated links or a whole router at once, while services crossing them are fine.
  - When a link goes down, its traffic moves to neighbours (their utilisation rises), and services crossing it see loss at the start.
- A missing one-hop latency probe while counters still report means the probe failed, not the link.
- When status polling is not available, telemetry absence plus traffic moving to neighbours is the main evidence of an outage.
"},{"runbook":"RB02_link_down","score":5.202,"text":"# RB02 Link down

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"}]}

Fault type: link_down. Root: a link.

Symptoms:
- The interface is reported down (link_status_down) when status polling exists.
- Telemetry on the link stops or reads zero: utilisation at 0 with the one-hop latency probe missing, or no data at all when status events are not available.
- Short loss on services that crossed the link while routing converges, then latency changes on the services that were rerouted.
- Neighbouring links (sharing a router) pick up the traffic: utilisation rises on them.

Checks:
- Is there a planned outage ("down") or drain on this link in the change log? If so it is maintenance, not a fault.
- Are many links blanked at the same time? That points to a collector gap (see RB09), not a link failure.

Action: open a fault ticket with the carrier or field team for the link; confirm rerouting has capacity.
"},{"runbook":"RB07_routing_misconfig","score":4.504,"text":"# RB07 Routing misconfiguration (link metric change)

Fault type: routing_misconfig. Root: the link whose routing metric was changed.

Symptoms:
- Traffic moves suddenly at one step: utilisation drops on one link and rises on others (metric raised), or rises sharply on one link (metric lowered, pulling traffic onto it).
- No interface goes down. Service latency changes because paths changed.
- Unlike a drain, there is no matching entry in the change log.

Checks:
- Look for a step change in utilisation on one link with no outage and no logged change.
- If a link lost most of its traffic while staying up, and nothing is logged, the metric on that link is the likely root.
- If one link suddenly carries much more than the day before, check whether paths were pulled onto it.
